root.name: King's Pawn Game: King's Head Opening

overview: White plays 2.f3 to support e4 and open the f-pawn, but it blocks the g1-knight, weakens the e1-h4 diagonal and the king, and gives Black free development. Black usually replies 2...Nf6 or 2...d5 and takes the centre, with ...Qh4+ ideas if g3 is forced. The opening is a rare, passive try that is not played by strong players, and I am unsure of its theory so the notes are kept short.

white_ideas.idea: Support e4 with f3 and develop Nc3, Bc4 and Ne2
Build a classical centre with d4 later

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...d5 or ...Nf6 and ...d5
Use the weak e1-h4 diagonal and the loose king with ...Qh4+ or ...Bc5

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after ...d5 exd5 with White's f3 pawn blocking the knight

character.notes: White's early f3 weakens the king and can lose quickly to ...Qh4+ and ...Bc5 ideas, but Black can also play quietly.

soundness.notes: Positionally weakening; Black is comfortable at least, and strong players do not consider it fully sound.

structure.notes: The e-pawns face each other and ...d5 opens the centre early.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever choose it.

level.notes: Few moves to learn but White must avoid positional and king-safety problems.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...Qh4+ line
sublines_that_differ.how: Black develops the queen early but loses time; not the main line.

character.reason: Unclear; neither especially forcing nor solid.

soundness.reason: The f3 move weakens the king and gives Black an easy game.

structure.reason: Black takes the centre with ...d5 and lines open early.

level.reason: A rarity and Dubious, so not Beginner.

plans.reason: No recognised plan from the table fits.
